paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as Abaye’s father. He reports that this was the reading in Yuchasin, whereas “our reading” is Kayyalal. See that entry.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Yuchasin has the heading’s Billal reading; Hyman says his current text has כיילל, transliterated here as Kayyalal.

The whole Warsaw 1878–1882 Seder HaDorot Tanaim and Amoraim 702 entry explicitly writes Billal, father of Abaye, and the alternative כיילל with kaf. This corroborates those two forms and the reported relationship. Hyman’s specific attribution of Billal to Yuchasin remains his report: Yuchasin itself has not been freshly collated. The current note is retained verbatim and qualified on that point; the alternative-entry pointer stays unbound, with no canonical genealogy or identity admission.
